The note is incorrect: in Habermas, "law as medium" means formal, purposive-rational regulation that steers systemically integrated spheres (economy, state administration), while "law as institution" means law anchoring the normative, communicatively integrated lifeworld (family, culture, public sphere) in shared values and mutual understanding. The distinction tracks the tension between systemic steering and lifeworld solidarity, not press/broadcasting versus courts.
CONFIDENCE: 90
